gaps.case: Two copies of one event run at the same time. A retry arrives after 5 seconds while the first copy's handler is still running, and up to eight jobs run concurrently. Both copies pass the 'not in set' check before either inserts the id, so the event is processed twice.
gaps.evidence: src/queue.ts:8 and src/queue.ts:12-13; design.md:4-6 checks before the handler and inserts after it

gaps.case: The process crashes, or the insert fails, after the handler has credited the account but before the id is recorded. The next delivery is processed again.
gaps.evidence: design.md:5-6 records the id only after the handler finishes; design.md:12-13 rejects insert-first in one transaction

gaps.case: The dedup key is job.eventId, which is copied from the unsigned X-Event-Id header. A delivery without that header gets the id "", so after the first one every later event is skipped as a duplicate. A forged or altered header can also suppress a real event or let a duplicate through.
gaps.evidence: src/main.ts:13; docs/provider-events.md:5-6 says the event id is the body's id field and X-Event-Id is not signed; src/signature.ts:5

gaps.case: Refunds arrive as charge.refunded, but the only refund handler is registered as refund.created. Under the design's default, an event with no handler is acknowledged and recorded as processed, so every refund is silently dropped and never retried. charge.disputed is dropped the same way.
gaps.evidence: docs/provider-events.md:11-12; src/events.ts:7; design.md:8-9; spec.md:16-21 requires refunds to be recorded

gaps.case: The spec has no scenario for concurrent duplicate deliveries, a missing or forged event id, or an event type with no handler.
gaps.evidence: spec.md:9-12 covers only a retry that arrives after processing has finished

rethink.problem: Checking an in-memory set before the handler and recording the id after it is a check-then-act design, so it cannot be exactly-once with concurrent workers or a crash between the two steps, whatever scenarios are added. It also keys on an unsigned header and treats every unrecognised event type as done, which fails open and silently loses refunds.
rethink.alternative: Claim the event by inserting the signed body's id under a unique constraint in the same database transaction as the ledger write, and skip the event only when that insert conflicts. Treat an event type with no handler as not processed: do not record it, surface it, and map charge.refunded to the refund handler.

approach.reasoning: The duplicates come from the approach itself: an in-memory check before the handler and a record after it race under eight concurrent workers and the provider's 5-second retries. The unhandled-type default and the unsigned header key turn missed forms into silent wrong answers. An atomic insert-first claim on the signed id, with unknown types treated as unprocessed, removes both problems.
